title: Plural personal partitive pronouns
summary: Use meitä, teitä and heitä for a plural personal object.
objectives: Use meitä, teitä and heitä for a plural personal object.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Use meitä, teitä and heitä for a plural personal object.
These pronoun forms refer to several people. One person can wait for a group, so the object’s plural number does not require a plural verb.
Learn me → meitä (we → us), te → teitä (you → you, several people), and he → heitä (they → them). All teitä examples here address several people; polite singular address is outside this lesson.
keyPoints: Use meitä, teitä or heitä as the plural personal object in this taught verb pattern.

steps: Use meitä, teitä or heitä as the plural personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Odotat means “you are waiting for” and works as the verb. odotat comes from odottaa: odota- + -t, with tt → t.
meitä means “us” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of me is meitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
Use meitä, teitä or heitä as the plural personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Autan means “I help” and works as the verb. autan comes from auttaa: auta- + -n, with tt → t.
teitä means “you, several people” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of te is teitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
Use meitä, teitä or heitä as the plural personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
heitä means “them” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of he is heitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
Use meitä, teitä or heitä as the plural personal object in this taught verb pattern.
Kuuntelen means “I am listening to” and works as the verb. kuuntelen comes from kuunnella: kuuntele- + -n, with nn → nt and the e stem.
teitä means “you, several people” and works as the partitive pronoun used as the object of the action. The standard written partitive form of te is teitä; learn this pronoun form directly.

commonMistakes: Keep the object pronoun distinct from the subject pronoun.
Choose the object number from the people referred to, not the person doing the action.
